chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband dies, indeed there is no maintenance (nafaqah) for her.
ai.seo_question: Does a pregnant widow receive maintenance (nafaqah) from her deceased husband's estate during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a pregnant widow is not entitled to financial maintenance (nafaqah) during her waiting period (iddah), distinguishing this ruling from that of a non-pregnant widow. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often contextualized by the principle that her maintenance is subsumed within the broader concept of her waiting period or linked specifically to the pregnancy itself, rather than the marital bond which has ended. The narration underscores the precise legal boundaries of post-divorce or post-death financial obligations in early Shia legal tradition.
